title: Pack a colour
description:
Screens store a colour as three numbers from 0 to 255: red, green and blue. Graphics code often packs all three into one 32-bit number laid out as `0x00RRGGBB`.

Write four functions:

- `std::uint32_t pack(std::uint32_t r, std::uint32_t g, std::uint32_t b)` builds the packed colour
- `std::uint32_t redOf(std::uint32_t colour)`, `greenOf(...)`, `blueOf(...)` pull each part back out

```
r = 0xFF, g = 0x88, b = 0x00   ->   0x00FF8800
```

Shift a part into place with `<<`, combine with `|`. To read one back, shift right with `>>` and keep the low 8 bits with `& 0xFF`.

starter.solution.cpp:
#include <cstdint>

// Write pack, redOf, greenOf and blueOf here.

hints: Red sits 16 bits up, green 8 bits up, blue at the bottom: `(r << 16) | (g << 8) | b`.
To read green: move it down to the bottom with `>> 8`, then mask off everything above the lowest 8 bits with `& 0xFF`.
